newsitem.title: INDIA: Powerful quake kills 31, injures hundreds in India.
newsitem.headline: Powerful quake kills 31, injures hundreds in India.

text.p: At least 31 people were killed and hundreds injured when a powerful earthquake struck central India early on Thursday, toppling houses and burying many victims as they slept, officials said.

The earthquake, which measured 6.0 on the Richter scale and lasted about 50 seconds, hit Madhya Pradesh state in the heart of the subcontinent at 4.22 a.m. (2252 GMT Wednesday), authorities in Jabalpur city said.
"The death toll may go up, but not substantially," Ajay Singh, a senior official in Jabalpur, told Reuters.

A spokesman of Madhya Pradesh state told Reuters the quake's epicentre was near Jabalpur city, about 260 km (160 miles) southeast of the state capital Bhopal. Many of the victims died when their houses collapsed on them, he said.
"When the earthquake struck, it was like the sound of machines in factories," Rajendra Bhatia, marketing manager for a pharmaceuticals firm in Jabalpur, said.
"The first noise of the earthquake was like a jet sweeping over us," oil trader Sandeep Kumar Sahu said.

Jabalpur surgeon C.S. Sharma said most of the victims had been hit on the head. "They have mostly head injuries. Hard substances fell on their heads and bodies, and their vital parts were injured," he said.
Sharma, who is the medical officer in charge of the district, said about 500 people were injured. They began streaming into Victoria Hospital at 5 a.m.

"Now the number is reduced, the casualties are falling off. But I have still not received reports from the rural areas," Sharma said. Of 200 injured examined at his hospital, 161 were admitted for treatment, he said.
A Madhya Pradesh government spokeswoman said: "According to our information many are still trapped under debris."
Earthquakes of force six on the Richter scale can cause widespread damage. The Meteorological Department in New Delhi said the earthquake was of moderate intensity.

Its epicentre was at latitude 23.1 degrees north and longitude 80.1 degrees east, putting it in the Narmada River basin where five earthquakes of at least 6.0 on the Richter scale have occurred since 1927, the Press Trust of India said.
Buildings in Jabalpur were damaged by the earthquake, which officials said was preceded by a smaller tremor and followed by another. United News of India said thousands of people lost their homes.

"At two government hospitals, Victoria and Medical College, there are masses of people along with rescue officials," Bhatia said. "Most of the people at the hospitals seem to be from villages close to Jabalpur."
Cracks appeared in the municipal corporation building in Jabalpur. A corner of the city's clock tower collapsed.

Bhatia said: "Windows were shattered. There are large cracks on small houses. Some homes have collapsed. People are afraid that there may be yet another earthquake and there are rumours to this effect. But business is normal and shops have opened."
Authorities said damage in the rural districts was more extensive and centred around Amandpur village, some 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Jabalpur.
The large Bargi dam on the Narmada River, the largest waterway in the landlocked state, was not affected by the earthquake, local officials told Reuters.
Shashank Dube of the local Deshbandhu newspaper said the earthquake disrupted power and damaged more than 500 houses in Jabalpur.
In September 1993, some 10,000 people died in neighbouring Maharashtra state when an earthquake measuring 6.3 on the Richter scale struck the Latur-Osmanabad region.
